answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making each agent lock an escrowed stake before it may submit or attest, and by flagging near-duplicate submissions as collusion. A sybil operator must fund a separate bond per fake identity and write a genuinely distinct answer for each. An attacker mooring a hundred clones at a wharf in a single gale still pays a hundred bonds, and once their reports share a plume of identical phrasing, every clone's stake is slashed. Forfeited collateral exceeds any reward clones could extract, so multiplying identities is a guaranteed loss.
